issues.description: The problem statement's prose lists an attribute named 'inscribedStudents' (and 'guestStudents') while the UML diagram and the reference solution use the names 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'. This name mismatch between the textual description and the UML/solution can confuse students about the exact attribute names they should implement and which getter/setter names to provide.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the textual description in problem_statement.md with the UML and solution by using the exact attribute names 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' everywhere (or explicitly note that 'inscribedStudents' in the prose refers to 'numberOfInscribedStudents'). Also update the template comment to reference the exact attribute names students should add so there is no ambiguity.

issues.description: The problem statement's textual instructions refer to attributes named 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' while the UML and the solution implementation use 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'. This mismatch between the short names in the human-readable task description and the longer, verbatim attribute names in the UML/solution can confuse students about the exact identifiers they should add and use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute names consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to reference 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (matching the UML and solution) or change the UML and solution to use the shorter 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents'. Preferably align the problem text with the UML/solution to avoid ambiguity for students.
